subject: Continuity Stack: RTO/RPO tiers, escalation roster, and degression clause
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 13:02:00 -0000
Subject: Continuity Stack: RTO/RPO tiers, escalation roster, and degression clause
Attachments: redwood-sla-draft-v2.pdf (application/pdf), oncall-roster.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. As promised, attached is a focused draft that maps Acme's throughput and peak-window expectations to an SLA stack we think will be operationally safe and commercially straightforward. Quick highlights up front: 

- Anchors: 99.95% monthly uptime for Bronze, 99.975% for Silver, 99.99% for Gold.
- RTO/RPO: Bronze (RTO 4h / RPO 60m), Silver (RTO 2h / RPO 30m), Gold (RTO 30m / RPO 5m).
- Escalation roster: Regional on-call during business hours; 24/7 escalation path for Gold. Roster spreadsheet attached.
- Degression (stepdown) clause: tiered discounts applied for sustained committed spend; we propose a 5% stepdown on per-token pricing at $X committed volume, then additional 3% at next tranche. We include a 30‑day review clause to reset capacity thresholds if utilization is consistently under 60%.

Two asks: can procurement confirm whether Acme is comfortable with a 30‑day utilization review (vs. a quarterly cadence), and do you want the degression expressed as fixed % reductions or a per-tier credit schedule? We can move either way — both have different revenue timing profiles for you.

If that works, I suggest we lock the legal redlines and sign the pilot (30-day pilot, month-to-month thereafter) while you confirm the procurement language. Would you like a quick 30-minute review tomorrow?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

[Redwood Inference — Production-focused LLM inference | https://redwoodinference.com]

From: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@acmecloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Cloud Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:18:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Continuity Stack: RTO/RPO tiers, escalation roster, and degression clause

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear summary and the draft — useful. A couple quick clarifications from procurement and engineering: 

1) Degression: Procurement prefers a credit schedule tied to annual committed spend rather than discretionary percentage stepdowns that trigger mid-term. The ask would be: can you map the 5% / 3% into an annualized credit table (we share a target booking cadence)?

2) RTO/RPO for Bronze: engineering asked whether Bronze can have a 2h RTO for network-related incidents if we pay a small premium — they want the ability to avoid manual failover if we choose. Is that flexible?

3) Escalation roster: we need names for the regional on-call (for SOC/audit). Can you provide a stubbed roster with role titles and escalation SLAs rather than specific personal names?

Happy to review the draft with my legal colleague once you translate the degression mechanics.

Thanks —
Samir
Samir Kapoor, Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Cloud
samir.kapoor@acmecloud.com

Internal —

Quick notes on Samir's asks before I respond to Acme:

- Translate degression to an "annualized credit table" as procurement requested. Jordan, can you run two scenarios: A) front-loaded credits (higher in Q1) and B) even spread across the year? We need TCV and cash timing impacts.
- RTO tweak: engineering wants Bronze RTO to be optionally 2h for a small premium. Kimberly, propose a delta $/token for a 2h Bronze option (we can express as per-month add-on or per-token uplift).
- Roster: we should provide role-based stub (e.g., 'APAC Tier 1 on-call (Regional SRE team) – 60m escalation, EMEA Tier 1 – 60m, Gold 24/7 escalation to Senior SRE – 15m SLA'). Avoid personal names to satisfy audit request.

I can draft a revised PDF today and then send back to Samir with call options.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Continuity Stack: RTO/RPO tiers, escalation roster, and degression clause

Samir / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick notes. Attached is a revised draft (redwood-sla-draft-v2.pdf) that includes: 

- An annualized credit table (page 4) that converts the proposed 5%/3% stepdowns into credits applied over the 12-month period. We show two amortization profiles (front-loaded vs. even spread) — summary table at top.
- A selectable Bronze 'accelerated RTO' add-on: $Y/month per region or a token uplift of Z% (both options captured; legal friendly language included).
- Role-based escalation roster and wording for audit (no personal names). Escalation SLAs and on-call rotation cadence included in the roster spreadsheet.

Next steps I propose: pick a credit amortization profile and confirm whether Bronze should include the accelerated RTO add-on. Once you confirm those two points I will: 1) prepare an 'execution-ready' redline for legal, and 2) spin up a pilot SOW that pins pilot acceptance criteria (RTO/RPO tests).

Would 10am PT Wednesday work for a 30-minute call?

Best —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 16:41:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Continuity Stack: RTO/RPO tiers, escalation roster, and degression clause

Marissa —

Thanks — the revised draft looks good and the annualized credit table helps procurement's forecasting. We reviewed both amortization profiles: procurement prefers the "even spread" profile (predictable OPEX). Engineering greenlit the Bronze 2h optional RTO if we do the per-region monthly add-on (please draft the SOW language that frames this as an optional add-on to be enabled at enrichment time).

Procurement also asked that the degression credit schedule include a hard floor (no more than 10% credits total in year one). Is that something Redwood can commit to in the pilot SOW?

If so, we're ready to proceed to an execution redline and a pilot SOW. I'll loop legal on a DocuSign after we get the execution-ready doc.

Samir
